question: In the case of ammonia, the power consumpon per ton refrigeraon with wet compression as compared with that of dry compression is _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __10% less__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ammonia refrigeration systems__ are widely used in industrial refrigeration applications.
 
• In the case of wet compression, the refrigerant is allowed to be partially wet (a mixture of liquid and vapor).
 
• In dry compression, the refrigerant entering the compressor is completely in the vapor state.
 
• Wet compression systems tend to have a slight efficiency improvement compared to dry compression systems.
 
• The power consumption per ton of refrigeration in a wet compression system is 10% less than that of a dry compression system.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Wet Compression:**
 
 
• It involves compressing a mixture of liquid and vapor refrigerant.
 
• This method can provide better cooling efficiency in certain systems.
 
 
 
• **Dry Compression:**
 
 
• Involves compressing only vapor refrigerant.
 
• Ensures that no liquid enters the compressor, preventing possible damage.
 
 
 
• **Ammonia as a Refrigerant:**
 
 
• Ammonia (NH₃) is a natural refrigerant with high efficiency.
 
• It is environmentally friendly and has zero ozone depletion potential.
